players.product: Optical fiber, optical fiber cables (high-fiber-count, ribbon, micro cables) and data centre connectivity products such as fiber-optic cable assemblies and patch panels

quarterly_data.signal: MD Mahendra Nahata (Q2 FY27 call): consolidated revenue INR 2,541.79 crores, up approximately 143.62% year on year and 32.73% quarter on quarter; EBITDA INR 658 crore (+223.55% YoY), margin 25.89%; profit before tax INR 538.60 crores (+406.49%); profit after tax INR 394.22 crores (+448.14%); export growth of approximately 493% year on year. He said growth came from both volume and price, and that 'there are no diamonds falling down from the sky' - no one-off high-margin business in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 2,541.79 crores (+143.62%); EBITDA margin 25.89%; PAT INR 394.22 crores (+448.14%)

quarterly_data.signal: MD Mahendra Nahata (Q2 FY27 call): HFCL now expects FY2027 revenue growth of at least 80% (the aspiration was approximately 20% at the start of the year, revised to 40% after Q1), says it is always good to be conservative, and would not be surprised to reach INR 10,000 crore revenue well before FY 2029; he expects revenue growth again in Q3 and margins to improve further. Connectivity solutions revenue is expected at about INR 800 crore this year (about INR 300 crore in Q2, nil in Q1) and INR 2,000 crore next year; defence revenue INR 500 crores to INR 600 crores this year, at least INR 2,000 crores next year and an aspiration of around INR 5,000 crores in three years; the EPC segment's loss over the next two quarters together should not exceed INR 75 crores to INR 100 crores, with profit from the first quarter of next year.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 revenue growth at least 80%; connectivity INR 800 crore FY27, INR 2,000 crore next year; defence INR 500 crores to INR 600 crores

quarterly_data.signal: MD Mahendra Nahata (Q2 FY27 call): order book INR 28,900 crores; within the INR 18,500 crore optical fiber cable and data center order book 'maybe 70%' of export orders could be from hyperscalers, while domestic orders are mostly from telcos; orders of about INR 5,500 crore were received in the quarter against about INR 2,500 crore supplied; contracts run from four to six months up to four years; HFCL is already delivering against its large hyperscaler order and has other hyperscaler orders; the aerospace business being acquired (completion expected this quarter) brings an order book of approximately INR 1,600 crore. Telcos are returning, with concrete inquiries for large orders.
quarterly_data.figure: order book INR 28,900 crores; about INR 5,500 crore of orders in the quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and supply (Q2 FY27 call, MD Mahendra Nahata): fiber runs at 100% of capacity and cable effectively at 100% in revenue terms, with data center products running 24 by seven; there are no preform supply challenges because HFCL buys on pre-determined long-term contracts, while market preform prices have gone up by 600% ('insane', he expects them to come down as capacity rises); fiber prices rose about 20% in Q2 and he sees them more or less stabilizing. Planned investment of approximately INR 1,800 crore takes fiber from 28 to 34 million fiber kilometers and cable from 34 to 63 million fiber kilometers; the 600 ton preform plant (October 2028 timeline, after 2-3 months of machine delays) will cover roughly half of fiber needs, a midterm own-preform solution starts in the first quarter of next calendar year, and germanium supply for two years from now is being discussed with suppliers.
quarterly_data.figure: fiber utilization 100%; cable capacity 34 to 63 million fkm; market preform prices up 600%

quarterly_data.signal: Market and product views (Q2 FY27 call, MD Mahendra Nahata): he sees no slowdown in data-center demand despite higher rates; growth is concentrated in North America and should pick up in Europe and Asia including India, where he expects data-center capacity of about 1.6 gigawatts today to reach 6 gigawatts or more by 2030; data centers are about 65%-75% of revenue and telcos 25%-35%; data-center fiber (G.657A2, 180 micron) sells at about $25 versus about $15 for telco G.652D fiber; HFCL's connectivity products are used inside data centers with the required certification. Defence: a second batch of thermal weapon sights for AK203 rifles was delivered to the Indian Defence Forces in September; a foliage penetration radar is in final trials; HFCL bid for 800,000 multi-mode hand grenades to be made at its planned ammunition complex on 1,000 acres in Andhra Pradesh.
quarterly_data.figure: data center 65%-75% of revenue; data-center fiber about $25 vs about $15
